newsitem.title: USA: US corporate bond market at standstill, eyeing Fed.
newsitem.headline: US corporate bond market at standstill, eyeing Fed.

text.p: Corporate bond new issue activity should remain at a virtual standstill as U.S. Federal Reserve policy makers meet on Tuesday, dealers said.
"Everyone's just waiting to get this (FOMC) meeting over with," said one syndicate source. "The market's at a standstill right now."
The Federal Open Market Committee, the policy setting arm of the Federal Reserve Board, meets on Tuesday to decide whether or not to raise official U.S. interest rates.
Meanwhile, in the absence of an official calendar, players remain sidelined with all eyes fixed on the Fed as speculation mounts for a 25 basis points rate hike, dealers added.
A recent Reuter poll of economists showed 17 of 30 experts expect the Fed to raise rates at the September 24 meeting.

Of the remaining 13 respondents, seven projected a monetary policy tightening at the November 13 FOMC meeting, one called for a rate hike early next year and five saw policy unchanged in the foreseable future.
Turning to the high-yield sector, so far only Boyd Gaming Corp is expected to price $200 million in Ba3/BB seven-year notes via Salomon Brothers later this week.
Looking ahead, Petronas is expected to price $500 million in debt via joint lead managers Salomon Brothers and CS First Boston, in the upcoming weeks.
In the government market, the 30-year bond is off 4/32 at 96-15/32 to yield 7.03 percent compared with 7.02 percent at Monday's close.
